newsitem.title: USA: SEC's Maco urges caution on structured financings.
newsitem.headline: SEC's Maco urges caution on structured financings.

text.p: Paul Maco, director of SEC's office of municipal securities, on Friday urged municipalities that do structured financings to make sure they are not creating new securities that must be registered with the commission.
"There may be more than one security in ... structured financings," Maco told bond lawyers meeting here for the National Association of Bond Lawyers annual workshop.
"(That) means you have to find an exemption for each one" under the federal securities laws, Maco said.
"You start throwing different types of contractual arrangements for exempt securities together, you might end up with a package that is slightly different from the pieces you put in," Maco said.
"And you may have merged with something that no longer has an exemption" under the securities laws, Maco said.
Maco added that when municialities start "pulling" securities together, they may end up with "something called an investment company."
That may be the case "even though you don't have a board of directors floating around or a fund manager," he said.
"The definition of an investment company is very liberal," Maco said.

"We've been seeing" some confusion in this area, Maco said. "We hope you keep this in mind when you find yourself with a client. Remember, there's more to the securities laws than just disclosure (issues)."
